q: Explain in your own words the difference between a quantity and a unit. Give an example and write the value of the quantity.
a: A quantity is a measurable property, for example the length $l$. A unit is an agreed measure with which the quantity is compared, for example the metre. The value of a quantity is the numerical value times the unit: $l = 3.2\,\text{m}$. The numerical value 3.2 alone tells you nothing.
